feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the scope, progression, and public-sector specialization come through clearly. It is well written overall, but it is slightly repetitive and overly dense in places, which reduces impact and makes the structure feel less streamlined than it could.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and strategic scope.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scale indicators: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Writing is polished and professional, with a consistent executive tone and strong alignment between summary, skills, and experience.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; these sections overlap heavily and could be consolidated for sharper focus.  
- Add more outcome-based results beyond activity descriptions—e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption improvements, or campaign performance—to strengthen impact.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation/bullet formatting is inconsistent in experience entries; “Coleman DAVIS” in all caps feels stylistically inconsistent with the rest. No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets; tightening it will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct, active phrasing.
- Add one concrete scale signal from recent roles to increase specificity (for example, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, or 50+ publishers).
- Streamline the service list so it reads as a leadership profile, not a skills inventory.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers enterprise platforms and editorial systems that support complex, mission-driven organizations, including large-scale Drupal environments, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled search and content experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The long list of capabilities repeats content already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more concise, parallel phrasing; remove filler like “operations” where possible.
- Prioritize the most senior, differentiating strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and multimedia.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestreaming
- Keep style consistent: either use “and” throughout or “&” throughout; “livestreaming” is cleaner than “livestream operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” and “multimedia production” repeat almost verbatim from the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills’ “Public-sector and advocacy messaging.”
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing, standardizing style, and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it more credible and scannable.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in such as “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Standardize wording and punctuation: use consistent verb tense, serial commas, and “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot.”
- Make outcomes more concrete where possible: e.g., improved policy-content discovery, supported campaign growth, extended reach across channels.
- Trim generic phrases like “designed for continued campaign growth” unless you can specify scalability, reuse, or audience impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current NACo roles; keep this section project-focused and avoid repeating responsibilities already listed above.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider leading with it or adding similarly unique projects to reduce repetition.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consulting-level outcomes, transformation work, and 2–3 signature initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “build and refine,” “deliver”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows,” “launched campaign microsites,” “improved governance,” “led AI search initiative.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets focused on highest-impact work: digital systems/analytics, Drupal campaign experiences, cross-channel governance, AI search.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, toolkit downloads, publishing efficiency gains, search success improvements, stakeholder teams served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital systems, workflows and analytics” and “governance… across web, email, social” repeat themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- Specific project details on microsites and AI search also duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/organizational scope, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine scope + flagship achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add metrics for email/social growth, video production volume, cost savings from the in-house studio, or reporting efficiency gains from GA4/BigQuery/BI stack.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels…” with a more results-focused bullet on audience reach, engagement, or campaign performance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed… email newsletters/social platforms” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects; mention the build and organizational impact, not routine production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good scope, but the item reads softer than the more senior NACo role and overlaps with both the earlier and later entries. Tighten it around operational leadership, channel ownership, and any measurable growth or process improvements.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Led NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel distributed across digital platforms.”  
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations bullet: “Built cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows that improved coordination, consistency and execution across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; distinguish this role as scaling/formalizing the program.
- “Improved workflows” overlaps with the 2022–2024 governance bullet; keep this version focused on day-to-day editorial operations, not enterprise governance.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around higher-value leadership capabilities rather than generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector stakeholder engagement
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Stakeholder engagement” or “Mission-driven communications” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Keep terms aligned with recent experience: emphasize transformation, governance, and operations over broad “content planning.”
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g., “Digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat almost verbatim from the header and Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is vague and partially redundant with campaign/storytelling language in recent roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix for the target roles, but this item is too broad and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and reduce tool-list repetition.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from a raw platform list to a capability-led line: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search”
- Put Drupal and CMS modernization first, since they are most supported by recent NACo experience.
- Consider dropping WordPress unless it is important for target roles; it is not reinforced in recent experience.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows” or “CMS modernization for large, multi-publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and save full tool inventory for the technical section.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent NACo leadership work, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. Make this more outcome-oriented and leadership-level.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics Strategy, Reporting & Optimization**
- Replace the list with: **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis**
- Lead with strategic capabilities, then tools: this better matches seniority and recent experience.
- If you have metrics, add one impact cue elsewhere in experience, e.g. “built analytics infrastructure supporting reporting for a 10,000+ page site and 3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure** and **Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization**.
- Consider keeping tools in **Technical + IT** and using this Topline Skills item for higher-level strengths only.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong and relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with work-experience bullets that already show studio buildout, livestreams, and video production. Make it more senior, operational, and event-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, higher-level phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • In-house studio operations • Virtual event production”
- Consider emphasizing leadership/ownership over tasks: “Studio and control-room operations” is stronger than “Studio operations.”
- If space allows, add scale or complexity rather than basic activities, e.g. “Broadcast-quality livestream and hybrid event delivery” or “Multi-camera livestream production.”
- Drop “editing” unless it is a differentiator for target roles; the CV already signals broad multimedia capability through experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with Core Competencies (“Multimedia & live event production”); keep this version more technical/tactical.
- “Video production” and “virtual event production” are already evidenced in multiple NACo roles, so avoid repeating broad wording.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution” and “Core Competencies.” This item should either be tighter or add light qualification by emphasizing strongest/current platforms first.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding proficiency framing: **Drupal (enterprise CMS, migration/redesign) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make it more outcome-linked and senior: **Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; avoid mixing “Web Platforms & CMS” here with broader technical capabilities listed elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider trimming one of the two.
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so this item should stay platform-specific rather than repeat scope.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools most relevant to recent Drupal/platform modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript, API integrations, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop versioning unless required: use “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” instead of “HTML5, CSS3”
- Consider grouping by function for clarity: Front-end (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • Integrations/Tagging (API integrations, Google Tag Manager) • Deployment/Automation (Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions)
- If accurate, add scope/outcome in a parenthetical: e.g., “API integrations, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions for CMS enhancements, analytics tagging, and deployment automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may partially overlap with GitHub Actions; differentiate as deployment automation/dev workflow.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a generic tool dump. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” in Topline Skills, so it should be tightened and framed around systems/automation rather than listing every collaboration app.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by function for faster scanning: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Consider trimming lower-value/general tools if space is tight; keep the platforms most tied to recent work and systems-building.
- If possible, add light proficiency/context elsewhere, e.g., “Built workflow automation and editorial coordination systems using Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language here.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; they add less differentiation than automation/project-system platforms.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platform list, but it’s too bare and undersells a clear strength area from recent NACo roles. Make it more specific and aligned to enterprise email operations, while avoiding repeating newsletter/channel leadership already covered in Work Experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add capability keywords instead of only tools: **campaign automation, segmentation, newsletter operations, audience journeys**
- Example rewrite: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Email campaign automation, audience segmentation, newsletter operations, member engagement workflows**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in recent Work Experience.
- Don’t repeat broad “multi-channel communications” language already covered in the summary and core competencies.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is currently a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” It would be stronger if framed around analysis and decision support rather than repeating product names already validated in recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Tighten and group terms: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- Replace vague **Dashboarding** with outcome-oriented language like **KPI reporting** or **executive dashboards**
- If space allows, align with recent impact by adding a qualifier: **enterprise analytics reporting** or **decision-support dashboards**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping tools here and moving broader capabilities there.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid expanding this into another full competency statement.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and anchor it in “firsts,” team-building, and concrete outputs.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout and production impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates for member and advocacy communications.”
- Tighten the management line: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate and helped formalize team workflows.”
- If possible, add metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, publishing volume, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this item framed as launching/establishing the format, not expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is echoed in later roles; use lighter wording here to avoid repetition.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the launch and scope, and trim broad support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the distinctive achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer outcome-oriented clause, e.g., “produced multimedia and digital content that supported program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scale or output: number of podcast episodes, audiences reached, projects supported, or types of stakeholders/programs served.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression is clear; one compact sentence or two bullets is enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/multimedia roles; avoid repeating broad production language.
- “Supporting organizational programs and policy work” is too generic unless tied to a specific initiative or result.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mixed capability summary than a clean tools line. It also overlaps with stronger, more recent multimedia leadership already shown in work experience and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten to software/tools only, and move workflow-style items to a different section if possible.
- Rewrite as: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Podcast editing/production**
- If livestream capability must stay, make it tool-oriented: **Broadcast/studio production workflows** instead of “Livestream studio workflows.”
- Only keep this item if these tools are relevant to target roles; otherwise shorten further to avoid over-weighting older hands-on production work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Podcast production” is already supported by the 2013–2015 role; avoid emphasizing it here unless it remains current.
- “Livestream studio workflows” overlaps with Core Competencies and Topline Skills (“Multimedia production and livestream operations,” “Studio operations”).
